Q: Convert lists of Coordinates to Polygons with GeoPandas A:
  1. Read the csv into a pandas dataframe
  2. Convert the string into a list and pass is to shapely.geometry Polygon
import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import Polygon
csv = r"C:\GIS\GIStest\fence.csv"
df = gpd.pd.read_csv(csv, sep=";")
df["geometry"] = df["FENCE_LOC"].apply(lambda x: Polygon(eval(x)))
df = gpd.GeoDataFrame(data=df, crs=4326).drop(columns=["FENCE_LOC"])
df.plot()

Q: ThenInclude() does not appear to work with ToList() A:

ToList() should't be the cause of the issue. Instead, most likely the cause is the discrepancy between the configured one-to-one relationship between DescriptionLink and Description, and actual database relationship. When loading related data, EF relies on the model metadata, and for one-to-one relationships it expects both principal and dependent keys to be unique in the corresponding tables. Actually relational databases have no one-to-one relationship concept, the only difference with one-to-many is FK being backed up with unique constraint.

In this specific case, EF expects DescriptionLink.DescriptionId to be unique, hence would only load single navigation property per unique key in the data set. Which one depends on Where clauses and in general is undetermined. And if the actual table contains duplicate values (which happens when the table is not created using EF migrations generated from the model), all the navigation properties except one will be null.

To fix the issue, simply make sure the entity and database models match. If the key in the linking (referencing) table is not unique, then the relationship between the corresponding dependent (join) entity and the principal entity must be configured as many-to-one (or one-to-many if you look from the other side).

With all that being said, make DescriptionLink -> Description relationship model similar to the existing DescriptionLink -> Article, i.e. Article and DescriptionLink entities and fluent configuration unchanged, Description inverse navigation property changed from reference to collection

public class Description
{
    // [...]

    public int DescriptionId { get; set; }

    // [...]

    public List<DescriptionLink> DescLinks { get; set; } // <--
}

and the corresponding fluent configuration:

DescriptionLink.HasOne(dl => dl.DescriptionPart)
               .WithMany(de => de.DescLinks)
               .HasForeignKey(dl => dl.DescriptionId)
               .HasPrincipalKey(de => de.DescriptionId);

or (it's one and the same as the previous, but make sure to use one or another, not both):

Description.HasMany(de => de.DescLinks)
           .WithOne(dl => dl.DescriptionPart)           
           .HasForeignKey(dl => dl.DescriptionId)
           .HasPrincipalKey(de => de.DescriptionId);

Q: Reproduce n-ary `vmap` from unary A:

Yes, vmap is able to map over a common dimension of multiple arguments. For example:

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

def f(x: jax.Array, y: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
  """Function with shape signature ([a],[b])->[c]"""
  assert x.ndim == y.ndim == 1
  return jax.numpy.concat([x, y])

n, a, b = 5, 3, 4

x = jnp.zeros((n, a))
y = jnp.zeros((n, b))

z = jax.vmap(f)(x, y)
assert z.shape == (n, a + b)

Q: simple-java-mail with native image: No provider of jakarta.mail.util.StreamProvider was found A:

The com.sun.mail:jakarta.mail:2.0.1 workaround is a terrible fix. That artifact is the old pre-Angus all-in-one Jakarta Mail implementation, so combining it with Jakarta Mail 2.1.x and Angus mixes two generations of the implementation.

SJM 8.12.4 brings Jakarta Mail 2.1.x plus Angus Mail. Angus contains the required service provider:

META-INF/services/jakarta.mail.util.StreamProvider
    -> org.eclipse.angus.mail.util.MailStreamProvider

The problem is that the provider is not being retained/discovered in the Quarkus native image. the following should fix that:

quarkus.native.auto-service-loader-registration=true

Or as Quarkus extension registration if you prefer:

new ServiceProviderBuildItem(
    "jakarta.mail.util.StreamProvider",
    "org.eclipse.angus.mail.util.MailStreamProvider"
);

Using that jakarta-mail 2.0.1 only hides the real problem, which is the underlying native-image ServiceLoader and can result in unpredictable behavior you might only discover in runtime, dus to the mixing of different generations of implementations.

Q: Flutter Google Sign-In [16] Account reauth failed on Android — need help troubleshooting A:

I had the same issue. Basically the error is a wrong SHA-1 configuration. You will have 3 different SHA-1:

  1. Debug: Used by Android Studio, when you compile in debug mode.

  2. Upload: You need to create a new keystore before publish your APK to Google Play.

  3. Google Play: Google resign your APK with their own SHA-1 key when you publish.

You need to include to your Firebase or GCP, the SHA-1 keys depending on the compilation. Example:

  1. If you are developing and debugging only. Include the SHA-1 from debug:

  2. If you compile your APK in "release" mode, and install it manually in your phone, you must register the "upload" SHA-1 key.

  3. If you deploy your APK to Google Play, you need to look at the SHA-1 applied by Google and register it.

If you don't register the correct SHA-1 from your specific compilation, you will have the error: "[16] Account reauth failed".

PS: As you are using Firebase, remember replace your "google-services.json" every time when you change your SHA-1.
